description:
pkix-path-builder/src/lib.rs:195-200 — `Error::NoValidPath { tried, last_error: String }`. The variant rustdoc (lib.rs:171-194) explains:

> last_error is the [pkix_path::Error::Display] rendering of the last candidate's validation failure. It is carried as a String rather than a pkix_path::Error so [Error] retains its Hash derive…

What it does NOT say: **the format of that string is not stable across versions**. The `Display` impl for `pkix_path::Error` is free to change wording, punctuation, formatting, and embedded context across minor versions without breaking any documented contract.

Two predictable caller failure modes:

1. **Substring-matching.** A caller writes:
   ```rust
   Err(Error::NoValidPath { last_error, .. }) if last_error.contains("SignatureInvalid") => { … }
   ```
   This works today, breaks silently when pkix-path renames the variant or adjusts the Display rendering. Failure mode: latent, observed only when behavior diverges in production.

2. **Logging-pinned tests.** A consumer's test asserts the rendered string matches a snapshot. Snapshot drift on every pkix-path patch bump.

The doc already steers programmatic-match callers toward `build_path_candidates` + per-candidate `validate_path`. That's correct but not sufficient — it doesn't tell the caller doing **logging-only** consumption that they cannot pin tests to the string.

Required doc (on the variant): "`last_error` is intended for human display only. The format may change in any non-breaking release. Callers MUST NOT substring-match this field or pin tests to its exact rendering."

Related: PKIX-wnnn.5 covers the typed-inner-error question. This finding is the orthogonal "what callers must NOT depend on" docs concern. They should both be addressed together.
title: Error::NoValidPath.last_error string format stability is not documented
